title: Headless Claude Code with DD hooks: where the task report is, and the flaky lock test
body: In a headless run with DD's hooks (`claude -p ... --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-hook-events`), the agent's task report is the assistant text after its last tool call and before the Stop hook_response that adds context; the result event's text is the reply to DD's Stop capture request ("I'm not proposing a memory from this turn"). A blind judge handed that text penalises DD and learns the condition (seen 2026-10-07); taskReport in src/eval/agent/metrics.js cuts at the right place. Register the hooks from hooks/hooks.json, never by hand. In a fresh clone the telemetry lock test (`a write waits for another process holding the telemetry lock instead of failing`) is flaky under load: 5 of 80 runs of the 2026-10-14 trial failed it first and passed on the rerun; the runner records both outcomes (suite_first_passed, suite_flaky_tests) rather than counting it against the agent.
not_derivable: metrics.js implements the cut; why it is needed (the judge reading DD's Stop reply) and which test is flaky live only in the trial write-ups.

evidence.summary: taskReport stops at a Stop hook_response that adds context.
Caveats: the telemetry lock test is flaky under load.
